answer: Requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can transact turns identity into a priced resource: a Sybil attacker must fund each fake persona, so every new copy sends a ripple of cost through the attacker budget. A reputation prism then refracts that stake through verified work history — honest agents earn cheaper access over time, while a relic of past fraud stays attached to the stake and burns it on abuse. Fakes become expensive and traceable, not free.
